svg.aria-label: The hierarchy, a line's life from DRAM to L1 and back
svg.text: The hierarchy, a line's life from DRAM to L1 and back
Inclusive below the L2, exclusive above it. The same 64 B travels as a half of a 128 B line once it leaves the L1.
Five levels and the rules between them
measured path, cycle guesses in magenta
PIPT, hashed, inclusive of the L1s
L1 fill: 64 B in 17 cycles at 32 B per cycle. A dirty L1D
line is written back to the L2, which already holds a
L1I fills from the L2; a store to code needs an explicit
SLC hit: about 90 cycles, refills L2 and L1 and leaves
the SLC. A CPU miss never allocates here; an L2 victim
DRAM fill goes to L2 and L1 past the SLC without
touching it (two labs). A modified SLC victim is written
Inclusive below the L2: the L2 keeps every L1 line.
Exclusive above it: a line is in the SLC or in the L2,
load misses the L1D: utag and PA tag miss,
request to the L2, after the dTLB gave the
L2 miss: duplicate tags say no other L1 has
it; the coherence point asks the other
DRAM read may already be in flight
DRAM returns 128 B: both halves enter the
L2, the touched half the L1 (disputed)
the waiting load takes its bytes as the fill
passes; the bank write steals a cycle
later: evicted L1 → L2 (kept, inclusive), L2
→ SLC; a reload removes it from the SLC
48 B load + 32 B store per cycle
